summary: Rewrote the LinkedIn adapter after live DOM capture proved LinkedIn shipped a rebuilt feed: all classes are rotating hashes, data-urn and data-id are gone, no article elements, and the feed is virtualised into div[data-lazy-mount-id] wrappers that are display:contents. All five previous selector arms matched nothing, so matched=0 and nothing ever reached the backend. New selector matches [data-lazy-mount-id] [role=listitem] plus main [role=listitem], keeping legacy arms for accounts still on the old build. Targets the listitem card not the wrapper, because a display:contents element has no box and could never render a veil. Identity is now a platform-prefixed content hash since no urn survives. Body text is recovered from innerText line by line with chrome stripped, including the poster's headline which would otherwise inflate every boast score. scan() falls back to closest() for virtualised re-hydration. Replaying the real captured card shapes caught two bugs the invented fixtures could not: company posts lost their entire body to the headline-drop rule, and bullet-prefixed chrome survived. 67 tests pass, verified end to end against live app.py.

summary: Wired the extension to the real app.py. Root cause found: a stray mock-backend was bound to :8000 alongside python app.py and, being the later binder, was answering every request - so all scores on screen were fake. Killed it, moved mock default to :8001, made it exit on EADDRINUSE, and added a popup warning banner when the reached backend self-reports as a mock (backend.status.service). Also closed the real wire gap: app.py returns a ragebait block (our own TF-IDF+LogisticRegression clickbait model from ML_part blended 0.6/0.4 with outrage heuristics) that decide.js was discarding - now a first-class REASON.RAGEBAIT with its own popup slider, veil label, event field and dashboard bar. Calibrated the threshold against the LIVE backend over a 28-post corpus: shipped 0.60 not app.py's 0.55, because at 0.55 ordinary technical questions flag (CI question scores 0.590) - the model was trained on headlines where an interrogative is itself a bait marker, so real quiz-bait at 0.598 sits 0.008 above a genuine question. No wide safe plateau; 0.60 catches 7/12 baits with 0 false positives. Added scripts/e2e-backend.mjs (npm run e2e) which runs the extension's own classify()+decide() against the live backend over 8 known posts and exits non-zero if a mock answers. 101 smoke tests pass (was 90); e2e verified against toxic-bert + MiniLM + Falconsai + the clickbait model, all 8 cases matching expectation.
